narrative:
Your loan application was denied because our system identified you as a potential bad credit risk, with a 51% chance of not repaying the loan. This decision was based on several key factors from your financial profile, which we compared to typical approved applicants.

The most important factor was the status of your checking account, which showed a negative balance (below 0 Deutsche Marks). This is a strong warning sign, as most approved applicants—about 50%—had no balance issues, while only 20% had negative balances. This pushed the decision toward denial.

Your credit history also played a major role. You have no credits or all paid off, which sounds positive, but this actually worked against you. Only 2.3% of approved applicants had this profile, while most had existing paid credits or a history of managing other loans. The model saw this as a lack of proven credit management, further contributing to the denial.

On a positive note, your property status—owning real estate—helped your case. This is a strong asset, as about 31% of approved applicants also own real estate, and it pushed the decision slightly toward approval. However, it wasn’t enough to overcome the other concerns.

Other details also mattered. You requested a loan of 1,108 DM for repairs, which is a less common purpose (only 1.9% of approved applicants used it for repairs). Your employment duration of 4-7 years is stable, but your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the average of 2.94% for approved applicants, suggesting tighter finances.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a positive credit history by taking and repaying smaller loans or using a credit card responsibly. Also, work on maintaining a positive checking account balance and consider reducing your installment rate by lowering the loan amount or extending the repayment period. These steps will show lenders you can manage credit effectively.
